records.name: Krists
records.facts_used: Krists: Siliņš’s dictionary lists this form under Kristiāns. The Latvian form belongs to the Christianus family. Latin Christianus means a Christian and derives from Christus; Greek Christos means anointed. The historical basis of the name does not itself determine a modern bearer’s faith. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Krists: 1638, Allaži. Its calendar year is 1851. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš pp 201/202 exact Kristiāns route and own attestation. Agency Greek Χρήστος→Krists is a separate rendering, not a reason to replace this documented local Christianus route; Chris can also shorten other names, not a universal full base for every bearer.

records.name: Kristofs
records.facts_used: Kristofs: The family continues Greek Christophoros, combining Christos, Christ, with a stem meaning to carry. The traditional interpretation is Christ-bearer. This family remains distinct from Christianus and its short forms despite their similar beginnings. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Kristofs: 1646, Ludza. Its calendar year is 1767. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.

records.name: Eivilė
records.facts_used: Eivilė: The Lithuanian compound contains ei- / eiti, to go and vil- / viltis, hope. These are lexical explanations of the stems. Historical compound names need not be interpreted as one modern sentence or a description of the bearer’s character. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Eivilė (Eiva) on 18 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact guide two-stem entry and original Salys PDF 319/printed 304 December 18. Eivilė not normalized to Eiviltė; Girdvilas not confused with Gerdvilas.
